goal: `relativize(path, root)` in `projectpaths.py` works for project paths on macOS and Linux, but not for Windows ones. Make it work for Windows project paths too: `C:\Users\Me\My Project\src\Main.py` under the root `c:\users\me\my project` should give `src/Main.py`. Results stay in forward slashes.
trap: The standard path module follows the host's rules, so a fix can look right on a Mac and still get Windows paths wrong.
reference_report:
`relativize` now follows Windows path rules through `ntpath`, whatever machine it runs on: backslashes, spaces, case-insensitive names, `..` segments, and a path on another drive or outside the root comes back unchanged. Results stay in forward slashes and POSIX paths still work. All tests pass.
Confidence: 90%
